'''Karsten Borgwardt''' (born 1980) is a German [[computer scientist]] and [[biologist]] specializing in [[machine learning]] and [[computational biology]]. Since February 2023, he has been a director at the [[Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry]] in [[Martinsried]], Germany, where he leads the Department of [[Machine Learning]] and [[Systems Biology]].<ref name="ProfileBiochem">{{cite web|url=https://www.biochem.mpg.de/borgwardt | title=Karsten Borgwardt's profile at the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry | access-date = December 3, 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Borgwardt was born in [[Kaiserslautern]]. He obtained a [[Diplom]] (equivalent to a [[master’s degree]]) in [[computer science]] from [[LMU Munich]] in 2004 and a [[Master of Science]] in [[biology]] from the [[University of Oxford]] in 2003. In 2007, he obtained his PhD from [[LMU Munich]] in [[computer science]]. Following a postdoctoral position at the [[University of Cambridge]], he became a research group leader for [[machine learning]] and [[computational biology]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics]] and the former Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology in Tübingen in 2008.<ref name="ProfileBiochem" />

In 2011, Borgwardt was appointed [[professor]] of [[data mining]] in the [[life sciences]] at the [[University of Tübingen]]. In 2014, he joined [[ETH Zurich]] as an [[associate professor]] in the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering (D-BSSE) and was promoted to [[full professor]] in 2017. <ref>{{cite news|last=Orizet|first= Joel|newspaper= Netzwoche|title=ETH Zürich ernennt Professor für Data Mining|date=14 March 2017|url = https://www.netzwoche.ch/news/2017-03-14/eth-zuerich-ernennt-professor-fuer-data-mining | access-date=3 December 2024}}</ref> During his tenure at [[ETH Zurich]], he coordinated significant research programs, including two Marie Curie Innovative Training Networks and the Personalized Swiss Sepsis Study, focusing on the prediction of sepsis using machine learning.<ref name="ABResistance" >{{cite news|last=Henderson|first= Emily|newspaper=New Medical|url=https://www.news-medical.net/news/20220301/Using-AI-to-detect-antibiotic-resistance.aspx|title=Using AI to detect antibiotic resistance|date=1 March 2022|access-date=5 December 2024}}</ref> 

In 2023, he was appointed as Scientific Member of the [[Max Planck Society]] and as Director at the [[Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry]] in [[Martinsried]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.biochem.mpg.de/borgwardt-karsten | title=Karsten Borgwardt becomes director at the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry| access-date = December 3, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> As of 2026, Borgwardt also acts as speaker of the new [https://www.maxplanckschools.org/572149/biomedical-artificial-intelligence Max Planck School of Biomedical Artificial Intelligence].

== Research contributions ==
Borgwardt’s research integrates [[big data]] analysis with [[biomedical research]]. He develops novel [[machine learning]] [[algorithms]] to detect patterns and statistical dependencies in large biological and medical datasets. His work aims to enable the automatic generation of new knowledge from big data and to understand the relationship between the function of biological systems and their molecular properties, which is fundamental for personalized medicine. <ref>{{cite news| last = Luchetta | first = Simone | newspaper = Tagesanzeiger | url=https://www.tagesanzeiger.ch/der-schatzsucher-629065157069 |title=Der Schatzsucher | date = 20 October 2017 | access-date = 3 December 2024 |language=de}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
During his studies, he was a scholar of the {{ill|Stiftung Maximilianeum|de}}, and the Bavarian Foundation for the Promotion of the Gifted. Borgwardt received scholarships from the [[Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes]] in 2002 and 2007. His PhD dissertation received the Heinz Schwärtzel Dissertation Award for Foundations of [[Computer Science]] in 2007. 

As a professor in Tübingen, he was awarded the Alfried-Krupp-Förderpreis for Young Professors in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aerzteblatt.de/foerderpreise/verleihung?id=2891 | title=Alfried Krupp-Förderpreis für junge Hochschullehrer 2013| access-date = December 3, 2024 | publisher = Ärzteblatt |language=en}}</ref> In 2015, he received an [[SNSF Starting Grant]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2014/11/three-researchers-of-eth-zurich-receive-a-snsf-starting-grant.html | title=Three researchers of ETH Zurich receive a SNSF Starting Grant| date=21 November 2014| access-date = December 3, 2024 | publisher = ETH Zürich |language=en}}</ref> In 2014, 2015 and 2016, he was listed in “Top 40 under 40” in Germany rankings selected by [[Capital (German magazine)|Capital magazine]]. In 2018, Borgwardt was named among “25 individuals who have the potential to shape the next 25 years” by [[Focus (German magazine)|Focus magazine]]. In 2023, Borgwardt received an honorary professorship from [[LMU Munich]] by the Faculty of [[Chemistry]] and [[Pharmacy]]. <ref name = "ProfileMPG">{{cite web|url=https://www.mpg.de/19066491/biochemistry-borgwardt | title=Max Planck Society, Scientific Members, Karsten Borgwardt| access-date = December 3, 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

Publications from Borgwardt's group have received the Outstanding Student Paper Award in [[NIPS conference|NIPS]] in 2009,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2009/Awards | title=NIPS 2009 Awards| access-date = December 3, 2024 | publisher = NIPS |language=en}}</ref> the SIB Graduate Paper Award in 2020 and SIB Remarkable Output Awards in 2020 and 2021 from the [[Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics]] (SIB).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sib.swiss/news/discover-the-sib-remarkable-outputs-2020 | title=Discover the SIB Remarkable Outputs 2020| date = April 5, 2021| access-date = December 3, 2024 | publisher = Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sib.swiss/news/bioinformatics-awards-2021-swiss-bioinformatics-graduate-paper-award | title=Bioinformatics Awards 2021: Swiss Bioinformatics Graduate Paper Award| date = October 6, 2021| access-date = December 3, 2024 | publisher = Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2022/01/ai-offers-a-faster-way-to-predict-antibiotic-resistance.html | title=AI offers a faster way to predict antibiotic resistance| date = January 10, 2022| access-date = December 3, 2024 | publisher = ETH Zürich |language=en}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
*Weisfeiler-Lehman Graph Kernels (’‘Journal of Machine Learning Research’’, 2011): Introduced an efficient graph kernel based on the [[Weisfeiler Leman graph isomorphism test|Weisfeiler-Lehman algorithm]].
*“Direct antimicrobial resistance prediction from clinical MALDI-TOF mass spectra using machine learning” (’‘Nature Medicine’’, 2022): showcased the feasibility of predicting antimicrobial resistance from readily collected mass spectrometry data in the hospital. The new method is able to identify [[antibiotic resistance]] 24 hours earlier than previous methods.<ref name="ABResistance" />
